newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan premium unaffected by Nissan Life's woes.
newsitem.headline: Japan premium unaffected by Nissan Life's woes.

text.p: The Japan premium -- the extra cost Japanese banks pay for raising funds in the eurodollar interbank market -- was steady and was unaffected by news of the failure of a life insurance firm, traders said on Friday.
Traders said news that the Finance Ministry had ordered Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co to halt operations did not immediately lead to worries about Japan's financial system.
"I think the market has got used to such news (about trouble at financial institutions)," a city bank trader said.
The relative stability of Tokyo share prices prevented the Japan premium from widening, said a trader for a foreign bank.
"I thought the premium might widen if share prices had fallen sharply, but they didn't, and I don't expect the premium to begin widening immediately," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Falls in Tokyo share prices are considered negative factors for Japanese banks, as they can lead to losses in the banks' stock holdings.
Japanese banks are paying around 5.72 percent for one-month eurodollar deposits, about 0.03 percentage point above the prevailing date.
The premium has stood at around 0.03 percentage point to 0.06 percentage point in the last two weeks.
Fluctuation in the Japan premium has been mild ever since fund-raising pressure began easing towards the beginning of this month, the city bank trader said.

"The Japan premium usually does not rise that much except when fund-raising pressure strengthens due to seasonal factors, such as when the premium rises towards the end of a business year," the trader said.
The Finance Ministry said in a statement on Friday it ordered Nissan Life to halt all operations except for servicing current customers.
